• simlevesque寻求计算资源支持其DuckDB相关研究项目。

• godber认为将大数据限定在“单机可处理的最大数据集”范围内是有道理的。

• mehulashah指出过去技术选择有其现实需求，认为若数据能在一台旧MacBook Pro上处理，则应选择适合的方案，但也承认历史需求推动了分布式系统的发展。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于实时交互式分析与预计算分析的价值对比，以及不同技术选择的适用场景和动机。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是数据库选择不仅关乎技术性能，还涉及生态系统和商业动机等多方面因素。
• 历史背景和技术发展路径也是讨论的重要部分，尤其是过去技术选择的原因和现代技术的反思。

44027690.article_content:
The Lost Decade of Small Data?
Hannes Mühleisen
Published on
2025-05-19
Reading time: 9 minutes
TL;DR: We benchmark DuckDB on a 2012 MacBook Pro to decide: did we lose a decade chasing distributed architectures for data analytics?
Much has been said, not in the very least by ourselves, about how
data is actually not that “Big”
and how the speed of hardware innovation is outpacing the growth of useful datasets. We may have gone so far to
predict a data singularity in the near future
, where 99% of useful datasets can be comfortably queried on a single node. As
recently shown
, the median scan in Amazon Redshift and Snowflake reads a doable 100 MB of data, and the 99.9-percentile reads less than 300 GB. So the singularity might be closer than we think.
But we started wondering, when did this development really start? When did personal computers like the ubiquitous MacBook Pro, usually condemned to running Chrome, become the data processing powerhouses that they really are today?
Let's turn our attention to the
2012
Retina MacBook Pro
, a computer many people (myself included) bought at the time because of its gorgeous “Retina” display. Millions were sold. Despite being unemployed at the time, I had even splurged for the 16 GB RAM upgrade. But there was another often-forgotten revolutionary change in this machine: it was the first MacBook with a built-in Solid-State Disk (SSD)
and
a competitive
4-core 2.6 GHz “Core i7” CPU
. It's funny to watch the
announcement
again, where they
do
stress the performance aspect of the “all-flash architecture” as well.
Side note: the MacBook Air was actually the first MacBook with an (optional) built-in SSD already back in 2008. But it did not have the CPU firepower of the Pro, sadly.
Coincidentally, I still have this laptop in the
DuckDB Labs
office, currently used by my kids to type their names in a massive font size or watch Bluey on YouTube when they're around. But can this relic still run modern-day DuckDB? How will its performance compare to modern MacBooks? And could we have had the data revolution that we are seeing now already back in 2012? Let's find out!
Software
First, what about the operating system? In order to make the comparison fair(er) to the decades, we actually
downgraded
the operating system on the Retina to OS X 10.8.5 “Mountain Lion”, the operating system version that shipped just a few weeks after the laptop itself in July 2012. Even though the Retina can actually run 10.15 (Catalina), we felt a true 2012 comparison should also use an operating system from the era. Below is a screenshot of the user interface for those of us who sometimes feel a little old.
Moving on to DuckDB itself: here at DuckDB we are more than a little religious about portability and dependencies – or rather the lack thereof. This means that very little had to happen to make DuckDB run on the ancient Mountain Lion: the stock DuckDB binary is built with by default with backwards-compatibility to OS X 11.0 (Big Sur), but simply changing the flag and recompiling turned out to be enough to make DuckDB 1.2.2 run on Mountain Lion. We would have loved to also use a 2012 compiler to build DuckDB, but, alas, C++ 11 was unsurprisingly simply
too new
in 2012 to be fully supported by compilers. Either way, the binary runs fine and could have been also produced by working around the compiler bugs. Or we could have just hand-coded Assembly like
others have done
.
Benchmarks
But we're not interested in synthetic CPU scores, we're interested in
synthetic SQL scores
instead! To see how the old machine is holding up when performing
serious
data crunching, we used the
at this point rather tired but well-known TPC-H benchmark
at scale factor 1000. This means that the two main tables,
lineitem
and
orders
contain 6 and 1.5 Billion rows, respectively. When stored as a DuckDB database, the database has a size of ca. 265 GB.
From the
audited results on the TPC website
, we can see that running the benchmark on this scale factor on a single node seems to require hardware costing hundreds of thousands of Dollars.
We ran each of the 22 benchmark queries five times, and took the median runtime to remove noise. However, because the amount of RAM (16 GB) is very much less than the database size (256 GB), no significant amount of the input data can be cached in the buffer manager, so those are not really what people sometimes call “hot” runs.

主要讨论点：对一篇关于自然界长期地质痕迹的论文及其相关概念的讨论

不同观点：
• [gnabgib] 认为该论文非常易读，并分享了论文链接。他侧重于论文的可读性和学术价值。
• [adityaathalye] 引用了Silurian Hypothesis（志留纪假说）来表达对地质痕迹长期保存的感慨，特别是提到自然现象如冰川、海平面变化和侵蚀对地质痕迹的影响。他还通过引用网络讨论，幽默地指出鲨鱼作为一种长期存在的生物的独特性。
• [veunes] 则对论文中提到的“爪子”这一细节印象深刻，认为这一小解剖特征传递了丰富的信息。

补充讨论：
• [adityaathalye] 的评论中提到了自然现象如冰川和海平面变化，这暗示了他对地质痕迹如何在长时间尺度上受到环境影响的关注。
• 争议焦点似乎并不明显，但[adityaathalye] 对鲨鱼“永恒”存在的幽默评论可能引起不同读者的兴趣或质疑，因为它偏离了主要学术讨论，进入了轻松的网络文化领域。
• [veunes] 的评论聚焦于论文中的具体细节，显示出对解剖学特征在理解古生物方面的重要性。

总体来看，评论者们对论文的可读性、地质痕迹的长期保存以及具体细节（如爪子）展开了多角度的讨论。

data.title: Decibels Are Ridiculous
data.author: Ariarule
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： decibel（分贝）在不同工程领域中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持分贝的实用性**：
   - **简化计算**：分贝可以将乘法转化为加法，方便处理增益和衰减（例如，滤波器损耗和放大器增益可以直接相加）。
   - **处理极大极小值**：分贝可以方便地表示和处理数量级差异很大的数值，避免使用科学计数法或处理复杂的浮点运算。
   - **多种工程领域应用**：在RF工程、音频工程、雷达等领域，分贝提供了一个统一的标度，便于比较不同数量级的信号。
   - **历史惯性**：尽管分贝有其复杂性，但由于历史原因，它已成为行业标准，改变的成本高。

• **批评分贝的复杂性和不一致性**：
   - **单位不明确**：分贝的定义和使用在不同上下文中存在不一致，特别是相对和绝对测量的混用（例如dBm、dB(SPL)、dB(A)等）。
   - **电压与功率的混淆**：分贝在处理电压与功率时采用不同的比率（电压是20倍的对数，功率是10倍的对数），容易引起混淆。
   - **主观校准**：例如音频VU表的校准基于主观模型，历史上由BBC和一些美国公司定义，缺乏客观标准。

• **对分贝的矛盾态度**：
   - **理解难度**：尽管分贝在工程中广泛使用，但其概念和应用对新手来说可能过于复杂，尤其是不同单位之间的转换和使用。
   - **历史遗留问题**：尽管认识到分贝的某些缺点，但工程师们因历史原因仍继续使用它，类似于软件工程中的某些历史遗留协议和工具。

补充讨论：
• **具体应用实例**：
   - 分贝在音频工程中用于表示动态范围和音量变化，在RF工程中用于表示信号链路的增益和衰减。
   - 分贝在图像处理领域也有应用，例如峰值信噪比（PSNR）使用分贝作为单位。

• **争议焦点**：
   - 分贝的定义和表示不一致，尤其是相对单位和绝对单位的混用，导致理解和使用上的困难。
   - 分贝在电压与功率计算中的不同处理方式增加了混淆的可能性。

总结：

data.title: Dijkstra on Ada
data.author: cpeterso
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了Dijkstra对四种早期编程语言提案（红、绿、蓝、黄）的评价，这些提案最终演变为Ada语言，其中绿色提案获胜。Dijkstra对各提案的评价非常严厉：红色提案“既先进又落后，令人困惑”；绿色提案“技术无能，可能还带有不诚实”；蓝色提案“过于复杂”，“技术文档和销售话术混杂”；黄色提案“无可救药的混乱”。在被问及对Ada的看法时，Dijkstra表示Ada的混乱让他担忧西方安全依赖于此，并开玩笑说如果红军也采用Ada，他会感到更安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Ada和Rust编程语言的评价与争议，以及对历史上编程语言选择过程的讨论。

不同观点：
• [rini17] 认为现代Ada是合理且不过分冗长的，并将其与Java比较。同时，对Rust的未来表示担忧，质疑将遗留的DoD C代码用AI重写为Rust的潜在风险。
• [phtrivier] 希望看到更完整的评论，并顺便提到Dijkstra如果使用社交媒体可能会浪费时间与网友争论，暗指Dijkstra的个性可能导致不必要的争论。
• [cyco130] 提供了历史背景信息，指出Ada是从多个提案中选出的，其中绿色方案获选，红色方案是备选。
• [johnisgood] 表示需要更多背景信息，认为评论中对Ada的厌恶表达缺乏理由支持，要求更详细的解释。
• [ggm] 回忆Wirth可能在Ada早期候选阶段提出了Modula/Modula-2变体，并通过三点推理支持这一观点，指出Dijkstra可能批评了所有候选语言。

补充讨论：
• [zombot] 表示对讨论内容感到困惑，无法理解。
• [mcv] 评论Dijkstra言辞犀利。
• [hello_computer] 质疑Dijkstra是否对任何事物有正面评价。
• [f1shy] 请求更多背景信息，特别是关于其他颜色提案的内容。
• [Surac] 以幽默方式评论男性只能区分6种颜色，暗示讨论中的某些观点可能与性别刻板印象有关。

争议焦点：
• 对Ada和Rust语言的评价存在分歧，特别是对Rust未来发展的担忧。
• 对历史编程语言选择过程的具体细节和背景信息的需求与提供之间的矛盾。
• 对Dijkstra个性及其评论风格的个人解读和评价。

44057731.article_content:
Dijkstra was one of the reviewers of the fours language proposals which eventually lead to the language Ada: red, green, blue, and yellow (the winning proposal was green). Here are some quotes from each of the reviews:
red
“the proposal is both advanced and backward in such an incongruous manner that I am baffled”
green
“technical incompetence, probably enhanced by dishonesty”
“I tried to reconstruct from the documentation a coherent design philosophy, an effort in which I failed: the mixture between sense and nonsense remained baffling”
blue
“the blue language is unacceptably complex”
“these documents are a inextricable mixture of technical documentation and salestalk”
“if we see a crazy argument, are we then allowed to conclude that the authors are idiots?”
yellow
“an unsalvageable mess”
In a conversation with Andrei P. Ershov (Soviet computer scientist), when asked about his view on Ada, Dijkstra commented that “
Ada was such a mess that I shuddered at the thought that Western security would depend on it and that I would feel much safer if the Red Army were to adopt it as well.
” [EWD1057].

data.title: What Sam Altman Told OpenAI About the Secret Device He's Making with Jony Ive
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI及相关公司是否应开发消费者设备，以及其在消费市场或B2B市场中的潜力。

不同观点：
• [aucisson_masque] 认为Apple和Google在AI创新方面进展缓慢，而Microsoft通过与OpenAI合作，已经将ChatGPT等AI功能集成到Office和Paint等软件中，接触到数亿消费者。因此，OpenAI需要通过构建设备直接与消费者互动。
• [weinzierl] 质疑OpenAI是否会开发消费者设备，还是专注于B2B市场。他认为如果面向企业市场，可能不需要像Jony Ive这样的设计师。
• [HacklesRaised] 强调需要看到OpenAI实际展示其能力，而不仅仅是宣传。他认为现在应该是OpenAI用实际行动来证明其潜力的时候。
• [camillomiller] 提出了一系列质疑，包括OpenAI模型的输出质量、目标用户群体、市场兴趣以及其硬件和供应链经验是否足够支持成功推出基于ChatGPT的产品。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于OpenAI是否具备足够的资源和能力来成功进入硬件市场，以及其潜在市场是消费者市场还是企业市场。
• 有人认为Microsoft已经在软件层面成功将AI功能推向市场，因此OpenAI可能不需要自行开发硬件。
• 还有人指出，OpenAI需要用实际成果来回应外界的期望，特别是在硬件开发方面。

data.title: Obsidian Bases
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: Obsidian于2025年5月21日发布了1.9.0版本，引入了一个新的核心插件“Bases”，允许用户将笔记转化为数据库，支持自定义表视图、数据过滤和动态属性。新版推出了“Footnotes view”插件，改进了多项功能，如脚注管理、PDF导出和同步历史视图。此外，取消了对某些属性的支持，并进行了多项界面和编辑体验的优化。开发方面，更新了CSS、YAML处理和多项技术组件。当前Bases处于早期测试阶段，未来将加入更多功能和API支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Obsidian中的Bases功能替代Dataview的潜力及其实际应用

不同观点：
• [支持Bases替代Dataview] Bases被视为Dataview的优秀替代品，提供更好的支持和更简单的语法。此外，Bases计划支持Obsidian Publish，而Dataview从未支持此功能。然而，由于Dataview的开发停滞，用户对其未来发展感到担忧。[lordfrikk]
• [对数据迁移的关注] 一位用户表达了对类似工具Notion的担忧，尤其是数据迁移的困难，并询问Bases是否能够方便地附加文件到笔记中以增强数据的可迁移性。[smodo]
• [个人信息管理用途] 一位用户认为Bases类似于1Password，但用于非秘密信息管理，例如记录家庭成员的个人信息。该用户强调Bases的发现能力优于简单笔记。[dmazin]

补充讨论：
• [技术实现细节] 一位用户指出Bases使用带有.base扩展名的yaml文件，并提供了相关帮助链接。[burgerrito]
• [安装问题] 一位用户询问如何在Linux上下载最新版本的Bases，因为网站上仍然显示旧版本。[Loxicon]
• [期待尝试] 一位用户对Bases表示兴趣，并希望尝试查看.base文件的具体表现。[vancroft]

争议焦点：
• Dataview的开发停滞导致用户寻找替代方案，而Bases被视为一个有潜力的继任者，但用户对其具体功能（如文件附加和跨平台支持）仍有疑问。

总结：用户对Bases作为Dataview替代品表示了兴趣，尤其是其简化的语法和未来功能支持。然而，用户在文件附加和跨平台下载方面存在一些疑问，显示出对实用性和便利性的关注。

Bases lets you create custom table views to visualize and interact with data in your vault. You can filter your notes by properties and create formulas to derive your own dynamic properties.

data.title: JEP 519: Compact Object Headers
data.author: Skinney
data.article_summary: JEP 519 提议将紧凑对象头（Compact Object Headers）从实验性功能转变为正式产品功能。该功能最初作为实验性功能在 JDK 24 中引入，经过测试证明其稳定性和性能优越，包括在 Oracle 和亚马逊的生产环境中得到了验证。测试显示，启用紧凑对象头后，SPECjbb2015 基准测试的堆空间使用减少了 22%，CPU 时间减少了 8%，垃圾收集次数减少了 15%，且 JSON 解析 benchmark 运行时间缩短了 10%。因此，现在是将其从实验性功能升级为正式功能的时候。升级后，将不再需要通过命令行选项 `-XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions` 来启用该功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JEP 519 关于启用紧凑对象头（Compact Object Headers）的默认设置及其性能影响

不同观点：
• **nicktelford** 认为 JEP 519 没有默认启用紧凑对象头是不合理的。他认为大多数用户不会特意去启用该功能，如果该功能已经被确认为稳定且能提升性能，就应该默认开启。他还提到，JVM 过去因为需要复杂的标志来优化性能（尤其是GC配置）而声名狼藉，尽管现在有所改善，但 JEP 519 似乎在这一方面又开了一个倒车。

• **SerCe** 则指出，先前的 JEP 450 提供了更多关于该功能的实现细节。该功能已经在 Oracle 和亚马逊进行了广泛测试，包括整个 JDK 测试套件和亚马逊生产环境中的数百个服务。SerCe 认为，在大公司中，平台团队有更多的机会和资源来测试和量化性能改进，而这是其他人难以获得的。

• **hmottestad** 对 JEP 519 的性能结果表示赞赏，特别是提到 JSON 解析基准测试显示了 10% 的性能提升。不过，他并没有对默认启用问题提出质疑，而是更关注性能改进的具体表现。

• **kosolam** 提出了一个问题，即该 JEP 是否也能提高 GraalVM 原生镜像的可执行文件的效率。这表明他对该功能在不同环境或工具链下的适用性表示关注。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于 JEP 519 没有默认启用紧凑对象头，这引发了 nicktelford 对用户体验和易用性的担忧，而 SerCe 则通过实际测试数据来支持该功能的可行性和稳定性。
• 该功能的具体性能提升效果得到了 hmottestad 的肯定，尤其是在 JSON 解析基准测试中的表现。
• kosolam 提出了该功能在 GraalVM 环境下的适用性问题，这是一个值得进一步探讨的方向。

Issue

Summary
Change compact object headers from an experimental feature to a product feature.
Non-Goals
It is not a goal to make compact object headers be the default object-header layout.
Motivation
Compact object headers were introduced as an alternative object-header layout by
JEP 450
in JDK 24. Features of this size are best introduced carefully and gradually, so we introduced it as an experimental feature.
Since JDK 24, compact object headers have proven their stability and performance.
They have been tested at Oracle by running the full JDK test suite. They have also been tested at Amazon by hundreds of services in production, most of them using backports of the feature to JDK 21 and JDK 17.
Various experiments demonstrate that enabling compact object headers improves performance:
In one setting, the SPECjbb2015 benchmark uses
22% less heap space and 8% less CPU time
.
In another setting, the number of garbage collections done by SPECjbb2015 is
reduced by 15%
, with both the G1 and Parallel collectors.
A highly parallel JSON parser benchmark
runs in 10% less time
.
It is time to change compact object headers from an experimental feature to a product feature.
Description
Compact object headers are enabled in JDK 24 via the command-line options
$ java -XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions -XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders ...
The first option,
-XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions
, will no longer be needed once they are a product feature.
Testing
Compact object headers were subjected to massive testing as part of
JEP 450
, in addition to the testing mentioned
above
. No further testing is required.
Some tests currently supply the
-XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions
command-line option when enabling compact object headers. This will no longer be needed, so we will adjust these tests accordingly.
Risks and Assumptions
As discussed in
JEP 450
, future features may require additional object-header bits. We have already reserved four bits for
Project Valhalla
. If a need for even more bits arises then we can shrink compressed class pointers and identity hash codes even further, using techniques we have already prototyped in
Project Lilliput
.

data.title: Why does Debian change software?
data.author: tapanjk
data.article_summary:
本文解释了Debian对其打包软件进行修改的原因，主要包括以下几点：

1. **遵循政策**：软件需符合Debian政策，如配置文件位置、文档存放目录等。
2. **协同工作**：软件需相互兼容，可能需要调整执行位置或用户账户。
3. **移除“回传”代码**：出于隐私和安全考虑，移除绕过Debian打包系统进行更新的代码。
4. **修复漏洞**：在上游修复前解决漏洞，或将补丁反向移植到早期版本，特别是安全问题。
5. **法律合规**：不包含无法合法分发的部分，可能根据Debian自由软件指南移除非自由部分到“非自由”区。
6. **添加手册页**：当上游未提供时，Debian会自行添加。

感谢Jonathan McDowell的协助，文责自负。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Debian对软件代码的修改及其影响

不同观点：
• [TekMol] 支持Debian移除绕过其打包系统进行更新或“回传”的代码，认为这是保持系统稳定和安全的重要举措。
• [rmccue] 反对Debian对源代码进行修改，指出这些修改曾导致其维护的PHP库出现问题，且没有通知用户他们使用的是分支版本，也未与原开发者沟通。
• [jeroenhd] 质疑Debian对某些软件（如xscreensaver）的修改，认为这些修改可能是基于美学和个人偏好，而非技术需求。
• [galad87] 批评Debian在替换库（如FFmpeg）后未能充分测试，导致发布破损软件。
• [yoyohello13] 更倾向于使用Arch Linux，因为其依赖上游官方文档，避免了Debian修改上游代码带来的潜在问题。
• [commandersaki] 反对Debian在软件中加入自定义配置框架，认为这增加了不必要的复杂性，更倾向于保持上游的原生配置。

补充讨论：
• [lifthrasiir] 提到Debian历史上曾发生的OpenSSL私钥 entropy 问题，质疑Debian目前如何预防和缓解类似事件。
• [Affric] 询问Debian如何看待和缓解因修改软件而带来的风险。
• [JdeBP] 指出Debian在手册页处理上的问题，认为其将外部软件的手册页存于系统自己的源控制中，而非优先考虑将其贡献回上游。
• [frainfreeze] 提到Debian因法律问题移除某些软件包，并引用了相关讨论链接。
• [anthk] 提到OpenBSD也会对软件进行修改，但目的是为了安全和遵循POSIX标准。
• [hsbauauvhabzb] 询问各发行版维护者是否共享补丁、手册页、回传数据等信息，以及是否公开变更信息。
• [INTPenis] 分享其转向RHEL的经历，认为RHEL更少修改上游软件包，提供了更大的控制权，但也指出Fedora的一些政策（如默认编辑器）同样存在问题。

争议焦点：
• Debian对源代码的修改是否必要及其对软件稳定性和安全性的影响。
• 修改上游代码带来的潜在问题和额外工作量，以及与原开发者的沟通不畅。
• 不同Linux发行版在软件包处理和用户控制权上的政策差异及其优缺点。

44059411.article_content:
When I wrote
Why is Debian the way it is?
, a year and a half ago, I was asked to also cover why Debian changes the software it packages. Hereâs a brief list of examples of why that happens:
Software in Debian needs to follow certain policies as set by Debian over the years, and documented in the
Debian Policy Manual
. These are mostly mundane things like system wide configuration being in
/etc
, documentation in
/usr/share/doc
, and so on. Some of this is more intricate, like when names of executables can be the same in different packages.
Programs included in Debian need to work together in other ways. This might mean require changing one or both. As an example, they might need to agree where Unix domain socket exists, or what Unix user account they should run under.
Debian will remove code that âcalls homeâ or tries to update software in a way that bypasses the Debian packaging system. This is done both for privacy reasons, and because updating software without going via the packaging system is usually problematic from a functional point of view, and always problematic from a security point of view.
Debian may fix bugs before theyâre fixed in upstream, or may backport a bug fix to an earlier version. The goal here is to make life better for users of Debian. Debian does this especially for fixes to security problems, but also for other problems.
Debian avoids including anything in the main part of its package archive it canât legally distribute. This applies to the source packages. This means, Debian may strip out those parts software that it doesnât think are free according to the Debian Free Software Guidelines. The stripped-out parts might be moved to another package in the ânon-freeâ part of Debian. An example might a manual that is licensed under the GNU Free Documentation License with immutable parts, or a logo that canât be changed.
Debian has often added a manual page when the upstream doesnât provide one.
Thank you to Jonathan McDowell for help with this list. Opinions and mistakes are mine. Mine, I say!
44059411.article_summary:
本文解释了Debian对其打包软件进行修改的原因，主要包括以下几点：

1. **遵循政策**：软件需符合Debian政策，如配置文件位置、文档存放目录等。
2. **协同工作**：软件需相互兼容，可能需要调整执行位置或用户账户。
3. **移除“回传”代码**：出于隐私和安全考虑，移除绕过Debian打包系统进行更新的代码。
4. **修复漏洞**：在上游修复前解决漏洞，或将补丁反向移植到早期版本，特别是安全问题。
5. **法律合规**：不包含无法合法分发的部分，可能根据Debian自由软件指南移除非自由部分到“非自由”区。
6. **添加手册页**：当上游未提供时，Debian会自行添加。

感谢Jonathan McDowell的协助，文责自负。

data.title: Direct TLS can speed up your connections
data.author: tanelpoder
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了通过直接TLS加速数据库连接的方法。作者的团队发现，在使用公司VPN时，Aurora DSQL集群的连接速度很快，但不在VPN时则需要约3秒。经过调查，发现问题出在公司网络上。当客户端尝试建立TLS连接时，防火墙会尝试通过打开第二个连接来获取服务器证书，导致延迟。如果使用Postgres 17及以上版本，可以通过直接启动TLS协商来跳过额外步骤，从而加快连接速度。这解决了因防火墙规则导致的延迟问题。

How direct TLS can speed up your connections
A few months ago, one of my Aurora DSQL teammates reported a curious finding.
When connecting to their DSQL clusters using the corporate VPN, their
connections were fast and snappy - as they should be! But, when connecting
without using the VPN
, their connections were taking around 3 seconds.
Curiously, this was only happening when in the AWS offices.
Discovery
The trigger for this discovery was the public Preview of Aurora DSQL at
re:Invent 2024. Before the public release, access to DSQL had been restricted,
requiring developers to be on the corporate VPN. Developers started to interact
with DSQL off-VPN, and realized it was slower - way slower - than before.
What could possibly explain this? Clearly, it’s “the network” since that’s the
only difference. That doesn’t mean the office WiFi is slow - otherwise
connections would always be slow, instead of just off-VPN connections. But
something
about the office WiFi was adding significant overhead.
As it turns out, the office has three networks:
Both a WiFi and wired network for Amazon employees
A WiFi network for guests
One of my teammates did the following tests:
Network type
slow
Employee WiFi
yes
Employee wired
yes
Guest WiFi
no
So… there’s something specific happening
only on the corporate network
.
After doing some server-side debugging, the team noticed something strange. For
every connection being opened to the cluster, an additional connection was being
made. This second connection wasn’t even speaking Postgres!
How PostgreSQL does TLS
Reference:
Message Flow
from the Postgres 16 documentation.
To quote (with slight edits):
To initiate an SSL-encrypted connection, the frontend [Postgres client]
initially sends an SSLRequest message rather than a StartupMessage.
The server then responds with a single byte containing S or N, indicating that
it is willing or unwilling to perform SSL, respectively. The frontend might
close the connection at this point if it is dissatisfied with the response. To
continue after S, perform an SSL startup handshake (not described here, part of
the SSL specification) with the server. If this is successful, continue with
[…]
To anthropomorphize this:
client â server:
Hey, I’d like to talk to you, but first let’s setup TLS
server â client:
Sure, go ahead
client âµ server:
TLS handshake
client âµ server: [encrypted stream continues]
So, what we’re seeing in our logs is that the
first
connection does this, but
the
second
connection isn’t. The second connection was skipping ahead to step
3 and initiating a TLS handshake. Where is this second connection coming from,
and why isn’t it following protocol?
Cisco TLS Server Identity Discovery
After engaging with our corporate networking team, they shared the following
resource with us:
https://www.ciscolive.com/c/dam/r/ciscolive/us/docs/2021/pdf/BRKSEC-2106.pdf
This is awesome documentation, so if you’re into details, I’d recommend going
through it. Otherwise, here’s the summary.
The Cisco firewall has the capability to add rules based on the URL or
application being accessed. When you initiate a TLS connection, the client sends
a “hello” message to the server, and the server responds with some information
including its certificate. The firewall uses information present in the server’s
TLS certificate to enforce rules.
To really spell that out: the firewall sees the packets you’re sending and
receiving. When the client sends a
hello
, the firewall says “that looks like a
TLS hello”, and then waits for the server’s response. It inspects the
certificate and then applies any rules.
In TLS 1.3, the server’s certificate is encrypted, which means the firewall
can’t do this anymore. That’s what this slide deck is about.
TLS Server
Identity Discovery
is a feature that works around this problem. The firewall
will open a
second connection
and do a TLS 1.2 handshake to retrieve the
certificate in plaintext. If the rules allow the connection, the firewall then
allow the connection to proceed.
But, of course, that’s not what Postgres is expecting. Postgres is expecting
that clients who want to do TLS should first ask if the server supports it.
As it turns out, our firewall wasn’t configured to block unknown applications.
What was happening is the firewall
tried
to learn the certificate, then gave
up after 3s, allowing the original connection through. Mystery solved!
Direct TLS support
Here are those same Postgres docs again, this time on
version 17
. There’s new
content!
A second alternate way to initiate SSL encryption is available. The server will
recognize connections which immediately begin SSL negotiation without any
previous SSLRequest packets. Once the SSL connection is established the server
will expect a normal startup-request packet and continue negotiation over the
encrypted channel.
What this is saying is that if you’re using Postgres 17+ on both the server and

data.title: When a team is too big
data.author: gpi
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了团队规模过大时可能出现的问题，以及如何通过培养全能型人才提高生产力。作者以亲身经历为例，描述了一个14人团队在日常会议中遇到的沟通和效率问题，如信息过载、无关内容导致的分心和任务遗漏。为了解决这些问题，团队尝试了异步站会，但发现缺乏实时对话，效果不佳。随后，团队分成前端和后端两个专门小组，以提高相关性和协作效率。作者指出，全能型团队能减少内部依赖、瓶颈和单点故障，更具生产力和弹性，但全能型策略也有其局限性。文章强调了持续改进和环境准备对领导力的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：团队会议（standup）的有效性、团队规模与组成、专业化与全栈开发、办公室政治以及公开内容的使用限制。

不同观点：
• Etheryte认为，团队会议应该高效且有时间限制，每人不应超过一分钟，长时间的讨论应在会后进行。这需要主持人和参与者有纪律性，且指出瑞典文化可能导致不 confrontational 的会议风格。
• Teeray则强调团队会议的价值在于对话和协作，特别是解决阻塞问题，建议即时沟通而不是等待会议。
• Protocolture通过数据分析发现，小团队（如6名程序员）在同一空间内工作效果更好，而大团队（25名程序员）则面临管理困难。
• Bobek建议采用书面或异步的团队会议方式，认为这样更具协作性，并分享了一篇博文支持其观点。
• Makeitdouble指出，业务执行可能比技术知识更重要，但随着公司发展，更多的专业化可能带来更好的结果。
• Agge幽默地指出瑞典的披萨份量小，并认为3-4人的团队是一个理想的大小。
• Pards和Pc86讨论了禁止将内容用于机器训练的声明，Pc86认为这种限制是无效且不现实的。
• Mettamage认为，软件工程师应成为全栈开发者，学习不同领域的知识并不困难，尤其是对于受过计算机科学教育的人。
• Abhaynayar分享了个人职业发展中的困惑，希望从安全领域转向更广泛的技术领域如DevOps和云基础设施。
• FinnLobsien指出，不同类型的团队需要不同的人员和运作方式，如内部计费团队与初创公司增长团队的差异。
• Madaxe_again提到，当团队达到一定规模时，办公室政治成为一个不可避免的问题，并建议通过任务导向的团队轮换来解决。
• Cplan认为，文章中的解决方案类似于“DevOps”和“T型工程师”的概念，即具备广泛知识和某一领域的深度专业知识。
• I_love_retros认为文章结构混乱，没有明确说明大团队还是小团队更好。

补充讨论：
• 团队会议的时长和效率是讨论的焦点，有人认为应严格控制时间，有人则强调其对话和协作价值。
• 团队规模与管理难度之间的关系被多次提及，小团队被认为更高效。
• 全栈开发与专业化之间的平衡也是讨论的要点，不同职业阶段和背景的人对此有不同看法。
• 办公室政治在较大团队中被视为一个不可避免的问题，需要通过管理策略来缓解。
• 对公开内容使用限制的声明引发了对其实际效力和合理性的辩论。

Lately I’ve been thinking a lot about these questions:
What is a team?
How large is too large and how small is too small?
What qualifies a missions?
How to weigh the cons and pros of specialist vs generalist in the age of GenAI?
There’s a story for several years back that keeps back to my mind. What makes it interesting is the fact that there was no master plan. Yet with a few cultural elements, the story took such an interesting trajectory that it shaped my leadership model. Ever since, I have been an advocate of continuous improvement by preparing the environment instead of being the wise-ass who has the ultimate solution to all problems.
Today I want to tell that story with these key takeaways:
A generalist team is less likely to have internal dependencies acting as bottlenecks, blockage, and single point of failure. Generalist teams are more productive and resilient.
Handovers introduce the risk of misunderstanding, delay, miscommunication, and diluted accountability. Clear ownership requires knowledge, mandate, and responsibility. It’s easier to implement with generalists.
But as we’ll see generalism is not without problems either.
Subscribe
🤖🚫 Note: No generative AI was used to create this content. This page is only intended for human consumption and is NOT allowed to be used for machine training including but not limited to LLMs. (
why
?)
Story
Many yeas ago I was part of a large team. 14 members to be exact.
The problems started from the first standup: I didn't follow 90% of what everyone else was talking about. I thought it's because I'm new to the team but as time passed and I got closer to the other team members I learned that some others feel the same.
It wasn't unusual to see someone visibly yawn or fall almost sleep during the standup. There was at least something in the round of standup that was completely irrelevant and boring to a few.
In an effort to keep the standup short, we had a time limit per person paired with invented hand gestures to signal the person who is talking that their time is over.
We were 11 engineers which can still be fed on
2-pizzas
! Size wasn't the issue.
In fact, quite the opposite: every now and then we heard about a task that never came up during the standup and wasn’t in the backlog!
We learned about those phantom tasks as they were close to the finish line or after they ere delivered.
How did that happen? Usually, someone from another team or another part of the organization reached out for a friendly
favor
and since we had enough bandwidth and great engineers, they often did their best to help.
Async Standup
Later we switch to async standup. The implementation was simple: every workday a Slack reminder would pop up with a fixed message:
What did you do yesterday?
What will you do today?
Are there any impediments or do you need any help?
Each team member would write a comment more or less in line with what they would be telling at a sync (face to face) standup.
Those comments came in during the day, and some folks consistently missed it. Regardless, I rarely read all the comments because they were not relevant to what I was doing.
This was less disruptive than taking 30 minutes (less than 3 minutes per person) for the daily standup, which often dragged to 45 minutes and sometimes even an entire hour!
The async report turned to exactly that:
a report
.
The main value of a standup is to have a dialogue about blockage and spark opportunities to work together. Otherwise, it's enough to move issues on the Kanban swim lanes with a comment. That covers the reporting part. We missed a dialogue when a dialogue was due.
Concern-based Task Forces
I raised these issue in one of our retrospectives and the EM/PM said they'll take action.
The solution they came up with was to break the team into two halves:
The front-end "task force" (as it was called) would work on front-end stuff basically taking a Figma design and turning it to working UI.
The back-end task force would cover the rest from API, to CI/CD, and configuring cloud and operations.
The idea was to have smaller groups that would move faster, delivery independently, and are more relevant and connected to each other.
And we cut the team by tech, because anyone who has worked with engineers knows that they can be quite religious about their tools of choice. Back-end/Front-end seemed to be different enough to justify that cut.
The hypothesis was that front-end developers should care enough about each other's world and standup report. Similarly back-end task force should have some sort of interest and common language to hear each other and collaborate.

• Bobek建议采用书面或异步的团队会议方式，认为这样更具协作性，并分享了一篇博文支持其观点。
• Makeitdouble指出，业务执行可能比技术知识更重要，但随着公司发展，更多的专业化可能带来更好的结果。
• Agge幽默地指出瑞典的披萨份量小，并认为3-4人的团队是一个理想的大小。
• Pards和Pc86讨论了禁止将内容用于机器训练的声明，Pc86认为这种限制是无效且不现实的。
• Mettamage认为，软件工程师应成为全栈开发者，学习不同领域的知识并不困难，尤其是对于受过计算机科学教育的人。
• Abhaynayar分享了个人职业发展中的困惑，希望从安全领域转向更广泛的技术领域如DevOps和云基础设施。
• FinnLobsien指出，不同类型的团队需要不同的人员和运作方式，如内部计费团队与初创公司增长团队的差异。
• Madaxe_again提到，当团队达到一定规模时，办公室政治成为一个不可避免的问题，并建议通过任务导向的团队轮换来解决。
• Cplan认为，文章中的解决方案类似于“DevOps”和“T型工程师”的概念，即具备广泛知识和某一领域的深度专业知识。
• I_love_retros认为文章结构混乱，没有明确说明大团队还是小团队更好。

补充讨论：
• 团队会议的时长和效率是讨论的焦点，有人认为应严格控制时间，有人则强调其对话和协作价值。
• 团队规模与管理难度之间的关系被多次提及，小团队被认为更高效。
• 全栈开发与专业化之间的平衡也是讨论的要点，不同职业阶段和背景的人对此有不同看法。
• 办公室政治在较大团队中被视为一个不可避免的问题，需要通过管理策略来缓解。
• 对公开内容使用限制的声明引发了对其实际效力和合理性的辩论。

data.title: Hotspot: Linux `perf` GUI for performance analysis
data.author: jez
data.article_summary: Hotspot是由KDAB开发的Linux perf数据图形化分析工具，旨在为性能分析数据提供直观的用户界面，初期目标是实现类似KCachegrind的UI，围绕Linux perf工具进行可视化，并计划支持更多性能数据格式。它支持数据可视化、时间线过滤、记录数据等功能，并可通过AppImage在多种Linux发行版上运行。用户可以通过包管理器或AppImage安装Hotspot，还可以从源代码构建以获取最新版本。使用时，需先通过perf记录数据，然后用Hotspot打开生成的perf.data文件进行分析，支持命令行和图形界面操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开发者对不同性能分析工具的评价和使用体验

不同观点：
• [gue-ni] 提到 Firefox 也支持加载 'perf' 报告，并提供了相关链接。该评论主要是分享额外的一个工具，没有过多评价。
• [ognarb] 推荐了 Heaptrack 工具用于调查内存使用情况，并提供了相关链接，认为该工具对内存分析非常有帮助。
• [directmusic] 主要从事 macOS 开发，使用 Instruments 进行性能分析，但在 Linux 上更常用 Hotspot，并对其表示高度推荐。
• [fransje26] 对 Hotspot 工具给予高度评价，认为其易于使用，并与 perf 工具配合良好，尤其提到在 QtCreator 中的无缝集成体验。
• [dustbunny] 表示对 Hotspot 使用上有些困惑，转而使用了 speedscope，并考虑重新尝试 Hotspot。
• [drewg123] 询问 Hotspot 是否具有类似 Vtune 的源代码视图功能，能够将周期/缓存未命中等归因于代码行。
• [wizzledonker] 强烈推荐 Hotspot，表示每天都在使用以解决代码瓶颈问题。
• [grandinj] 认为 Hotspot 是非常有用的工具，对其在优化 LibreOffice 中的贡献表示赞赏。
• [pjmlp] 简单表示对工具的赞赏和感谢。

Hotspot - the Linux perf GUI for performance analysis
This project is a
KDAB
R&D effort to create a standalone
GUI for performance data. As the first goal, we want to provide a UI like
KCachegrind around Linux perf. Looking ahead, we intend to support various other
performance data formats under this umbrella.
Table of Contents
Screenshots
Visualizing Data
Time Line
Record Data
Getting Hotspot
ArchLinux
Debian / Ubuntu
Gentoo
Fedora
For any Linux distro: AppImage
Building Hotspot
Using
Off-CPU Profiling
Embedded Systems
Import Export
tracepoints
Disassembler
Known Issues
Broken Backtraces
debuginfod
Missing Features
Recording with perf without super user rights
Export File Format
Qt Creator
License
Screenshots
Here are some screenshots showing the most important features of Hotspot in action:
Visualizing Data
The main feature of Hotspot is the graphical visualization of a
perf.data
file.
Note: Inlined functions have a darker border than non-inlined ones.
Time Line
The time line allows filtering the results by time, process or thread. The data views are updated accordingly.
Record Data
You can also launch
perf
from Hotspot, to profile a newly started application
or to attach to already running process(es). Do take the
caveats below
into account though.
Getting Hotspot
Note: Hotspot is not yet packaged on all Linux distributions. In such cases, or if you want to use the
latest version, please use the AppImage which will work on any recent Linux distro just fine.
ArchLinux
Hotspot is available in AUR (
https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/hotspot
).
Debian / Ubuntu
Hotspot is available in Debian (
https://packages.debian.org/hotspot
) and Ubuntu
(
https://packages.ubuntu.com/hotspot
).
Gentoo
Hotspot ebuilds are available from our overlay (
https://github.com/KDAB/kdab-overlay
).
Fedora
Hotspot is available in Fedora (
https://packages.fedoraproject.org/pkgs/hotspot/hotspot/
).
For any Linux distro: AppImage
You can either head over to the most
current release
or the
continuous build
.
In both cases you'll find the AppImage under "Assets" that you can download.
Untar the AppImage file (in case of the latest release), then make it executable and then run it.
Please use the latest build to get the most recent version. If it doesn't work, please report a
bug and test the latest stable version.
Note: Your system libraries or preferences are not altered. In case you'd like to remove Hotspot again,
simply delete the downloaded file. Learn more about AppImage
here
.
To find out how to debug the AppImage, see
HACKING
.
Building Hotspot
Building Hotspot from source gives you the latest and greatest, but you'll have to make sure all its
dependencies are available. Most users should probably
install Hotspot
from the distro
package manager or as an
AppImage
.
For everyone that wants to contribute to Hotspot or use the newest version without the AppImage detailed
notes are found at
HACKING
.
Using
General
First of all, record some data with
perf
. To get backtraces, you will need to enable the dwarf callgraph
mode:
perf record --call-graph dwarf
<
your application
>
...
[ perf record: Woken up 58
times
to write data ]
[ perf record: Captured and wrote 14.874 MB perf.data (1865 samples) ]
Now, if you have Hotspot available on the same machine, all you need to do is launch it.
It will automatically open the
perf.data
file in the current directory (similar to
perf report
).
Alternatively, you can specify the path to the data file on the console:
hotspot /path/to/perf.data
Command Line options
Depending on your needs you may want to pass additional command line options to Hotspot.
This allows to one-time set configuration options that are found in the GUI under "Settin

data.title: Single RGB camera turns your palm into a keyboard for mixed reality interaction
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 中国清华大学团队开发了一种名为Palmpad的技术，利用单个RGB摄像头和Arduino实现混合现实中的交互。用户可以在手掌上看到投影的小型键盘，并用另一只手的食指点击虚拟按键。通过复杂的视频帧处理技术和卷积神经网络，系统能精准定位食指相对于手掌的位置。同时，利用Arduino UNO Rev3监测手掌间的电信号，检测手指与手掌的接触，实现97%的触控识别准确率。该技术解决了此前指尖追踪和触控检测不准确的问题，为混合现实交互提供了新方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Palmpad触摸识别技术的可行性、实用性以及与其他技术的比较。

不同观点：
• rspoerri：认为Palmpad的触摸识别准确率达到97.0%，可靠性较高，但在需要大量打字的情况下完全不实用。
• yaris：提到了多年前见过的两种项目，一种是使用可穿戴相机和彩色标记来识别手势，另一种是使用陀螺仪传感器识别手指和手部运动。认为这些项目很有趣，但之后没有再听说。
• GoblinSlayer：建议参考《加速世界》中的增强现实（AR）键盘，通过显示在用户面前的虚拟键盘来解决问题。
• alexisread：认为Palmpad虽然看起来不错，但实际上依赖于单个RGB相机和大量的处理能力。指出需要高性能的图形处理，并且在减少分辨率和帧率的情况下仍需解决处理延迟和与头戴设备集成的问题。同时提到与和弦输入法相比，Palmpad在CPU需求、准确性、速度上都有所不足，显示出不同的权衡。

补充讨论：
• rspoerri的观点强调了Palmpad在实际应用中的局限性，特别是在打字等高强度输入任务中的不适用性。
• yaris提到了历史上的类似技术，暗示这些技术可能没有得到广泛应用或进一步发展，从而提出了Palmpad是否会有类似命运的问题。
• GoblinSlayer的建议提供了一种不同的解决方案，即通过AR技术来增强用户交互体验。
• alexisread详细分析了Palmpad的技术要求和现实挑战，包括处理延迟、与头戴设备的集成以及与其他输入法（如和弦输入法）的比较，揭示了技术实现中的复杂性和可能的权衡。

争议焦点：Palmpad在实际应用中的可行性和与其他技术的比较，特别是对于需要大量打字的任务的适用性。

Blog Home

VIGOR fuses fashion and technology in an avant-garde wearable
Blog Home
A single RGB camera turns your palm into a keyboard for mixed reality interaction
Arduino Team
—
May 9th, 2025
Interactions in mixed reality are a challenge. Nobody wants to hold bulky controllers and type by clicking on big virtual keys one at a time. But people also don’t want to carry around dedicated physical keyboard devices just to type every now and then. That’s why a team of computer scientists from China’s Tsinghua University developed interaction technology called
Palmpad that enables typing with just a single RGB camera and an Arduino
.
This isn’t a new idea, but the execution stands out. It works by pointing a camera at the user’s hands. In mixed reality, the user sees a small keyboard projected on top of their palm. They then use their index finger on their opposite hand to tap the virtual keys. The camera tracks the movement of the index fingertip relative to the palm to determine which virtual keys the user touches.
Previous attempts by others to implement this method have had limited success for two reasons: unreliable fingertip tracking and poor touch detection.
The Tsinghua University team solved the first problem with sophisticated video frame processing techniques, such as motion extraction, and with a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained for this purpose. Their system is able to determine the position of the fingertip relative to the palm with great accuracy.
They solved the second problem by using an
Arduino UNO Rev3
to monitor electrical signals being passed from one hand to the other. Those signals come from a waveform generator, which produces two very low-current, low-voltage AC signals at 12.5MHz. One is a reference and the other passes from an electrode on one hand to an electrode on the other hand. The Arduino monitors those signals through an analog multiplier and a low-pass filter, detecting a change in impedance indicating finger-to-palm contact.
Wherever the user’s fingertip is at that moment is the point registered as a “click.” The team reported a touch recognition accuracy of 97.0%, which makes Palmpad quite reliable.
More details on the Palmpad
can be found in the researchers’ paper
.
Image credit: He and Wang et al.

data.title: The Agentic Web and Original Sin
data.author: prawn
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了网络广告作为互联网主要商业模式的起源和影响。Ethan Zuckerman认为，广告是网络的“原罪”，导致用户数据被收集和操纵。Marc Andreessen则反思，未能将支付功能内置于早期网络浏览器是这一问题的根源。尽管广告模式有弊端，如用户隐私受侵和内容操控，但它有效地将人类注意力货币化，带来了巨大的经济价值。文章还指出，微交易模式因多种问题（如交易费用和用户体验）并不可行，而订阅模式更成功，因为它基于持续的价值交付，而非单次内容消费决策。总体而言，尽管广告模式有缺陷，但它在当前环境中是相对有效的选择。
data.comments_summary:

The Agentic Web and Original Sin
Tuesday, May 20, 2025
Listen to Podcast
Listen to this
post
:
Log in to listen
Ethan Zuckerman wrote in
The Atlantic
in 2014:
I have come to believe that advertising is the original sin of the web. The fallen state of our Internet is a direct, if unintentional, consequence of choosing advertising as the default model to support online content and services. Through successive rounds of innovation and investor storytime, we’ve trained Internet users to expect that everything they say and do online will be aggregated into profiles (which they cannot review, challenge, or change) that shape both what ads and what content they see. Outrage over experimental manipulation of these profiles by social networks and dating companies has led to heated debates amongst the technologically savvy, but hasn’t shrunk the user bases of these services, as users now accept that this sort of manipulation is an integral part of the online experience.
Marc Andreessen, who was there when the web was born,
explained in a 2019 podcast
why this sin was committed (
this quote is lightly edited for clarity
):
One would think the most obvious thing to do would be building in the browser the ability to actually spend money, right? You’ll notice that didn’t happen, and in a lot of ways, we don’t even think it’s unusual that that didn’t happen, because maybe that shouldn’t have happened. I think the original sin was we couldn’t actually build economics, which is to say money, into the core of the internet and so therefore advertising became the primary business model…
We tried very hard to build payments into the browser. It was not possible…We made a huge mistake. We tried to work with the banks and we tried to work with the credit card companies…it was sort of the classic kind of single point of failure bottleneck, or at least in this case, two points of failure. Visa and MasterCard essentially had a duopoly at the time, and so they were just literally, if they did not want you to be in the switch, they did not want you to be able to do transactions, you just simply weren’t going to do it.
I think Andreessen is too hard on himself, and I think Zuckerman is too harsh on the model Andreessen created the conditions for. The original web was the human web, and advertising was and is one of the best possible ways to monetize the only scarce resource in digital: human attention. The incentives all align:
Users get to access a vastly larger amount of content and services because they are free.
Content makers get to reach the largest possible audience because access is free.
Advertisers have the opportunity to find customers they would have been never able to reach otherwise.
Yes, there are the downsides to advertising Zuckerman fretted about, but everything is a trade-off, and the particular set of trade-offs that led to the advertising-centric web were, on balance, a win-win-win that generated an astronomical amount of economic value.
Moreover, I disagree with Andreessen that we could have ended up with a better system if the banks and credit card companies had been willing to play ball. In fact, over the last thirty years, the credit card companies in particular have — in part thanks to companies like Stripe — gotten their digital acts together, and are integral to a huge amount of web-based commerce, which itself is driven through digital advertising (the largest category of advertising for both Google and Meta). That too is human, in that the biggest outcome of digital advertising is physical products and real-world experiences like travel (digital products like apps and games, meanwhile, are themselves pursuing human attention).
What was not viable in the 1990s, nor at any time since then, was something like micro-transactions for content. One obvious problem is that the fee structure of credit cards don’t allow for very small transactions; another problem is that the costs to product content are front-loaded, and the potential payoff is both back-loaded and unpredictable, making it impossible to make a living. The biggest problem of all, however, is that micro-transactions are anti-human: forcing a potential content consumer to continually decide on whether or not to pay for a piece of content is alienating, particularly when plenty of alternatives for their scarce attention exist.
Subscriptions do work at smaller scales, because they are ultimately not about paying for content, but giving money to another human (or human institution); from
The Local News Business Model
:
It is very important to clearly define what a subscriptions means. First, it’s not a donation: it is asking a customer to pay money for a product. What, then, is the product? It is not, in fact, any one article (a point that is missed by the misguided focus on micro-transactions). Rather, a subscriber is paying for the regular delivery of well-defined value.
Each of those words is meaningful:
Paying
: A subscription is an ongoing commitmen

文章讨论了一种替代传统自回归模型的大语言模型方法，即基于Score Entropy Discrete Diffusion模型。尽管自回归模型（如GPT-2）在生成自然语言文本方面表现优越，但其基本方法百年未变，主要依赖于下一个词预测。新的扩散模型通过估计数据分布的比率，在保持高性能的同时，提供了独特的算法优势，挑战了自回归模型的主导地位。

传统概率建模包括数据收集、学习近似数据分布的参数化密度，并用其生成新样本。然而，自然语言的离散性和复杂性使得直接计算所有可能输入的概率不切实际。自回归模型通过分解序列概率解决了这一问题，但新方法提供了更具潜力的替代路径。

文章强调，Score Entropy Discrete Diffusion模型不仅能有效生成复杂数据分布的样本，还可能引领基于不同原理的语言模型发展。

44058950.article_content:
Language Modeling by Estimating the Ratios of the Data Distribution
Modern large language models (like ChatGPT) learn to generate new samples by modeling the data distribution of natural text. However, the underlying methodology has largely remained stagnant over the last century: although different architectures have been developed, models are all based on autoregressive modeling (i.e. next token prediction). In this blog post, I will talk about our work on Score Entropy Discrete Diffusion models, an alternative probablistic modeling technique that achieves highly competitive performance (at the scale of GPT-2) while introducing distinct algorithmic benefits. Our empirical results challenge the longstanding dominance of autoregressive modeling and can potentially pave the way for an alternative class of language models built from radically different principles.
Introduction
At the core of modern generative AI systems lies the field of probabilistic modeling. The idea behind probabilistic modeling is surprisingly straightforward and consists of three steps:
Collect a dataset \(x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n\) which we assume has been sampled i.i.d. from our underlying data distribution \(p_{\mathrm{data}}\).
Learn a parameterized density \(p_{\theta}\) (often using a neural network) such that \(p_{\theta} \approx p_{\mathrm{data}}\). For example, we could use our dataset to minimize the negative log likelihood loss: \(\begin{equation} \mathbb{E}_{x \sim p_\mathrm{data}}[-\log p_\theta(x)] \approx \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i = 1}^n -\log p_\theta(x_i) \end{equation}\)
Use \(p_\theta\) to generate new samples. Bonus points if we can sample conditionally \(p_\theta(\cdot \vert c)\) (where \(c\) is something like a prompt, desired property, etc…).
For a data domain such as natural language (which this blog post focuses on), things seem like they should be easy. In particular, our data is
discrete
, meaning that the support of \(p_{\mathrm{data}}\) lies on a finite set \(\mathcal{X} = \{1, \dots, \vert\mathcal{X}\vert\}\). For the simple examples we might find in a standard undergraduate probability textbook, we can directly learn the probabilities of each element:
A probability density function for the sum of two dice rolls. One could directly learn the values of $p_\theta(2)$, $p_\theta(3)$, ..., $p_\theta(12)$ with a maximum likelihood estimator given some samples.
Unfortunately, real world datasets are much more complex than this. For something like natural language, we are working with something like the
Library of Babel
, where all possible combinations of characters must be analyzed. This makes things quite a bit more challenging.
For natural language, we need to calculate $p_\theta$ for exponentially many inputs.
To overcome this challenge, we use a parameterized model (like a neural network) to map values to probabilities \(p_\theta: \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}\), but our troubles are not over yet. In particular, constructing a valid probability density \(p_\theta\) requires two mathematical conditions:
\[\begin{equation} p(x) \ge 0 \quad \text{ and } \quad \sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} p(x) = 1 \end{equation}\]
Since neural networks \(f_\theta\) (by construction) output general values, enforcing these conditions requires additional constraints. For example, one could build an
energy based model
:
\[\begin{equation} p_\theta(x) = \frac{e^{f_\theta(x)}}{Z} \quad \text{ where } \quad Z = \sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} e^{f_\theta(x)} \end{equation}\]
But, for this type of parameterization, computing \(Z\) is near-impossible due to the curse of dimensionality (forcing one to rely on crude approximations). For example, for something like GPT-2, computing \(Z\) would requiring evaluating \(p_\theta\) for all \(50257^{1024}\) different possible input sentences (this is a number far greater than the number of atoms in the known universe).
Autoregressive Modeling
Luckily for us, there is a way to make this problem tractable. In almost all practical applications, our data support \(\mathcal{X}\) is highly structured, factorizing into a product set \(\mathcal{X} = \{1, \dots, N\}^d\) so that elements are given by \(\mathbf{x} = x^1 x^2 \dots x^d\). For real world examples, this would break down a sentence (“The red dog ran.”) into its constituent parts (“The”, “red”, “dog”, “ran”, “.”). Because we instead model sequences \(x^1 x^2 \dots x^d\), we can decompose using the probablistic chain rule:
\[\begin{equation} p_{\mathrm{data}}(x^1 x^2 \dots x^d) = p_{\mathrm{data}}(x^1) p_{\mathrm{data}}(x^2 \vert x^1) \dots p_{\mathrm{data}}(x^d \vert x^1 \dots x^{d - 1}) \end{equation}\]
This motivates
autoregressive modeling
, which instead seeks to learn each component probability \(p_\theta(x^i \vert x^1 \dots x^{i - 1}) \approx p_{\mathrm{data}}(x^i \vert x^1 \dots x^{i - 1})\). As a result, this is often colloquially called next token prediction. Compared with the naive approach, this is extremely scalable since each component probability’s normali

data.title: SUS backprop: linear backpropagation algorithm for long inputs in transformers
data.author: brandonb
data.article_summary: 本文提出了一种名为SUS backprop的线性反向传播算法，用于处理Transformer模型中长输入的计算问题。针对注意力机制在长序列中计算需求随序列长度平方增长的问题，作者设计了一种概率规则，通过单个参数$c$控制，在反向传播时仅保留每个token在每个注意力头中最多$c$个交互，从而将计算复杂度从$O(n^2)$降至$O(nc)$。实验表明，对于典型Transformer模型，剪除99%的注意力梯度流仅导致相对梯度方差增加约1%，且该方法适用于稀疏矩阵实现，有助于在处理长序列时显著降低训练成本。

Title:
SUS backprop: linear backpropagation algorithm for long inputs in transformers
Authors:
Sergey Pankov
,
Georges Harik
View a PDF of the paper titled SUS backprop: linear backpropagation algorithm for long inputs in transformers, by Sergey Pankov and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
It is straightforward to design an unbiased gradient estimator that stochastically cuts the backpropagation flow through any part of a computational graph. By cutting the parts that have little effect on the computation, one can potentially save a significant amount of back-propagation computation in exchange for a minimal increase in the stochastic gradient variance, in some situations. Such a situation occurs in the attention mechanism of the transformer architecture. For long sequences, attention becomes the limiting factor, as its compute requirements increase quadratically with sequence length $n$. At the same time, most attention weights become very small, as most attention heads tend to connect a given token with only a small fraction of other tokens in the sequence. These weights become promising targets for cutting backpropagation. We propose a simple probabilistic rule controlled by a single parameter $c$ that cuts backpropagation through most attention weights, leaving at most $c$ interactions per token per attention head. This brings a factor of $c/n$ reduction in the compute required for the attention backpropagation, turning it from quadratic $O(n^2)$ to linear complexity $O(nc)$. We have empirically verified that, for a typical transformer model, cutting $99\%$ of the attention gradient flow (i.e. choosing $c \sim 20-30$) results in relative gradient variance increase of only about $1\%$ for $n \sim 2000$, and it decreases with $n$. This approach is amenable to efficient sparse matrix implementation, thus being promising for making the cost of a backward pass negligible relative to the cost of a forward pass when training a transformer model on long sequences.

44058294.article_summary: 本文提出了一种名为SUS backprop的线性反向传播算法，用于处理Transformer模型中长输入的计算问题。针对注意力机制在长序列中计算需求随序列长度平方增长的问题，作者设计了一种概率规则，通过单个参数$c$控制，在反向传播时仅保留每个token在每个注意力头中最多$c$个交互，从而将计算复杂度从$O(n^2)$降至$O(nc)$。实验表明，对于典型Transformer模型，剪除99%的注意力梯度流仅导致相对梯度方差增加约1%，且该方法适用于稀疏矩阵实现，有助于在处理长序列时显著降低训练成本。

data.title: ChatGPT Is a Gimmick
data.author: blueridge
data.article_summary:
这篇文章描述了作者参加的一次关于人工智能教学的研讨会经历。作者原本期望不高，但因学生使用AI生成论文而感到迫切需要找到解决方案。研讨会的主讲人是一位曾主张移除课堂数字技术的大学前校长，但他却在会上让参会者使用大型语言模型（LLM）进行操作，导致注意力分散。演示中，AI生成的作文缺乏明确的论点，而后的播客总结也显得浅薄无聊。主讲人过度热情地展示AI的各种功能，给人一种急于推销技术的感觉。

文章还提到《高等教育纪事报》上的一篇文章，作者斯科特·拉瑟姆设想了一个由AI“代理”全程指导学生从入学到就业的未来，声称这将更好且更便宜，但忽视了AI的高成本和环境代价。文章最后总结，AI并非革命性技术，而是一种噱头，虽然承诺减轻繁重工作，但最终令人失望。大学如轻信这些炒作，可能会付出沉重代价。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（如ChatGPT）和AI工具的实际效用与局限性，以及它们是否只是噱头。

不同观点：
• alkonaut认为，ChatGPT等LLM在处理复杂问题时容易迎合用户的假设，而不是挑战它们，导致错误答案。他指出LLM缺乏对答案的自信评估能力，认为这是当前技术的一大缺陷。
• keiferski则持相反观点，认为AI工具（如ChatGPT和Midjourney）提供了巨大的价值，尤其是在创意和生产力提升方面。他强调不应将AI视为解决一切问题的“魔法按钮”，而是灵活运用以实现特定目标。
• danlitt支持alkonaut的观点，表示自己也很难从LLM中获得有价值的答案，并质疑那些声称从AI中获得巨大收益的人是否只是自我欺骗。
• wiseowise以讽刺的口吻称所有新技术在初期都被质疑为噱头，但认为当前的LLM已经是“魔法”般的进步，尽管它们并不完美。
• ddxv指出，AI的炒作部分源于其演示效果，但这些项目往往成为死胡同，类似于网页模板，可以帮助起步但缺乏深度。
• elric关注AI对人际互动的影响，担心过度依赖AI会削弱人类之间的合作与交流。
• BlindEyeHalo认为LLM在取代谷歌搜索方面很有用，特别是在应对垃圾信息和繁琐的搜索结果时。
• blixt主张不应将AI简单地视为好或坏，承认其局限性同时也看到其潜在的创新应用。
• lexandstuff指出，AI的炒作部分源于AI自身生成的内容，导致技术界对AI的过度期望。
• panstromek推荐了一个更平衡的关于AI的讨论视频，以抵消原文中的悲观态度。
• bushbaba分享了个人经验，表示ChatGPT极大地提升了他的写作效率和工作质量。
• ohxh批评原文浅薄，认为不应因为个人无法获得良好输出就否定LLM的价值。
• mirekrusin承认AI带来的挑战，但总体持乐观态度，强调适应新技术的重要性，同时提醒不要过度依赖AI。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于AI工具的实际效用与过度炒作之间的差距。一些人认为AI是革命性的工具，而另一些人则认为其效用有限，且容易被高估。
• 讨论中多次提到AI不会取代人类劳动，但可以作为增强生产力和创造力的工具。
• 另一个值得注意的点是AI对人际互动的影响，有评论担心AI会削弱人类之间的合作与交流。
• 对于AI工具的应用，评论中提到应根据具体情境灵活使用，而不是将其视为万能解决方案。

44058677.article_content:
I recently attended a workshop on teaching with artificial intelligence at the university where I teach writing as a part-time adjunct. I had low hopes for the workshop, but I was also desperate. My students keep turning in essays that were obviously generated by AI, and I need to figure out what to do. I looked forward to hearing the keynote speaker, a former university president who made his name arguing that instructors should move all digital technology out of their classrooms so they and their students can focus on the human interactions that technology cannot replace.
At the workshop, though, the first thing he asked us to do was open our laptops, navigate to a couple of LLMs, and enter a prompt. As we did this, he kept talking. What was I supposed to pay attention to? Him, or my screen? While he jabbered, I prompted Claude.ai to write a short essay in response to one of the “innovative” topics it had proposed to me: a “Change My View Challenge,” based on a Reddit forum. It was important that I use the word
innovative
in my prompt, the presenter insisted. Omit
innovative
and you get different, presumably more pedestrian, results. Claude spat out the paper and told me it was proud of its work, which, after all, had a “clear thesis statement.” When I said I couldn’t find the statement, Claude replied, “You’re right to question this. Looking at the essay more carefully, there isn’t a single, explicit thesis statement that clearly states the central argument.” Thanks, genius.
Later, the presenter wanted to demonstrate the amazing feats of pedagogical customization AI is capable of. So he asked a model to create, on the spot, a brief podcast summary of his own book, adding that the model should employ baseball metaphors, because, in this experiment, the user is a jock who cares only about baseball. The idea seemed to be that students would better appreciate the book’s content if it were expressed in terms they are already familiar with. He pressed play. The resulting summary, offered by credibly bland digital hosts, was astonishingly shallow and stupid, wedding one tired cliché (education is “lighting a lamp”) to another (“beware of the curveballs”). Was anybody really learning anything from this?
The presenter seemed to be trying much too hard.
AI can do this! AI can do that!
He moved randomly from topic to topic, bouncing around the stage and making faux-shocked faces at his own pronouncements about the marvelous, career-disrupting implications of large language models. He seemed overstimulated and came across as impatient with the pace of human life and thought as it has been until now.
That speaker was not the most frenzied AI advocate I came across this spring. A recent issue of the
Chronicle of Higher Education
ran a fevered
fantasy
by one Scott Latham, a professor of strategy at the Manning School of Business at the University of Massachusetts at Lowell. It is a vision featuring AI “agents” that will provide students a bespoke experience running from orientation through course instruction to job placement, all the while tracking their every frown and furrowed brow (because students will stare endlessly into cameras) and responding at each moment with the perfect remedy. “Human interaction is not as important to today’s students,” Latham claims, and so presumably the AI university will offer little. Compared to the current model of college, he promises, all of this will be better and cheaper—never mind growing evidence that LLMs are deteriorating and becoming
more expensive
.
And it
will
happen. In fact, the word
will
appears more than 130 times in the 4,000-word article.
Could
, only twice. “Predicting AI’s disruption is the easy part,” Latham writes. “The tough part is making people realize the inevitable.”
The claim of inevitability is crucial to technology hype cycles, from the railroad to television to AI. “A key strategy for a technology to gain market share and buy-in,” the scholars David Gray Widder and Mar Hicks
write
, “is to present it as an inevitable and necessary part of future infrastructure, encouraging the development of new, anticipatory infrastructures around it.”
The infrastructure demanded by AI is neither neutral nor cheap. It has well-known environmental costs, given the vast amount of electricity and water its data centers demand. Nor is the infrastructure only physical. It has already been built in the minds of students, who are becoming informational lotus-eaters, addicted to immediate, effort-free homework answers and adequate-seeming essays on demand.
* * *
Tot up the overeager salesmen, the questionable prophecies, and the clearly exorbitant costs, and it becomes clear: AI is not revolutionary. It’s a gimmick. It entices us with the prospect of sparing us drudgery, but it ultimately disappoints.
AI apologists are like hucksters at a county fair, fast-talking about some newfangled marvel. Universities are their gape-mouthed marks,
emptying their pockets
even while they are

data.article_summary: 本文简要列出了与YouTube及相关服务的一些重要信息和功能。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者相关信息、广告、开发者条款、隐私政策、安全指南以及如何使用YouTube。此外，还提到正在测试的新功能和NFL Sunday Ticket服务，并注明版权为2025年归Google LLC所有。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：运行时环境与框架的区别，以及是否应使用纯HTML和CSS进行开发。

不同观点：
• [0xEF]认为“运行时环境”只是“框架”的另一种说法。他质疑如果有人想摆脱web框架的繁琐和冗余，为什么不直接使用纯HTML和CSS从头构建网站。这里表达的观点是对“运行时环境”这一术语的不满，并建议彻底放弃框架。

• 另一种隐含的观点是，运行时环境和框架是不同的概念。运行时环境指的是程序运行时所需的基础设施和资源，例如JavaScript引擎或Java虚拟机，而框架是一组用于简化开发的预定义工具和库。这种观点强调了两者在软件开发中的不同角色和功能。

补充讨论：
• [0xEF]的评论中还包含了对开发方式的建议，即使用纯HTML和CSS进行开发，以避免框架带来的复杂性。这涉及到对框架的评价，认为框架可能带来不必要的复杂性和冗余。

• 争议的焦点在于“运行时环境”和“框架”这两个术语的定义和使用，以及在实际开发中是否应完全避免使用框架。这反映了开发者在选择技术栈时的不同偏好和理念，一些人可能偏好轻量化的开发方式，而另一些人可能更看重框架提供的便利和功能。

• 另一个值得注意的点是，讨论涉及到开发效率和控制粒度之间的权衡。使用纯HTML和CSS可能提供更多的控制和简洁性，但可能在大型项目中降低开发效率，而使用框架则可能在提高效率的同时引入复杂性。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应依赖现有能源技术解决当前问题，还是期待未来技术（如核聚变）的突破。

不同观点：
• [ggm的观点]  
   1. 虽然现状令人遗憾，但在能源资金规划中必须明确当前可用的技术。  
   2. 当前应专注于大规模应用现有技术来解决碳排放问题，而不是寄希望于未来核聚变技术。  
   3. 核聚变技术在短期内无法帮助我们摆脱“碳陷阱”。

• [tomcam的观点]  
   1. 不同意ggm的观点，认为其看法是“无稽之谈”。  
   2. 根据其50年来对核聚变技术的关注，核聚变技术一直被描述为“还有5年就能实现”，并且这种说法非常稳定，意味着核聚变可能很快就能实现。  
   3. 暗示核聚变技术距离实际应用可能并不遥远，仍有期待的价值。

补充讨论：
• [争议焦点]  
   1. 争议的焦点在于是否应该依赖现有技术解决问题，还是继续等待未来技术（如核聚变）的突破。  
   2. ggm认为当前应该务实，专注于可大规模应用的现有技术，而tomcam则对核聚变技术抱有更乐观的态度，认为其可能在短期内实现。  
   3. 对于核聚变技术实现的时间预期存在明显分歧，ggm认为短期内不现实，而tomcam则认为一直以来都是“5年之遥”。

   2. ggm认为当前应该务实，专注于可大规模应用的现有技术，而tomcam则对核聚变技术抱有更乐观的态度，认为其可能在短期内实现。  
   3. 对于核聚变技术实现的时间预期存在明显分歧，ggm认为短期内不现实，而tomcam则认为一直以来都是“5年之遥”。

data.article_summary: 文章作者Joe Eklund对PG&E（太平洋天然气与电气公司）的不断涨价感到不满，决定自行安装太阳能系统以减少对PG&E的依赖。作者详细描述了选择太阳能系统的过程，包括研究各种技术选项和报价。他最终选择建立一个大型系统，以彻底消除高额电费。文章探讨了电池、逆变器和净能量计量（NEM）等技术细节，特别是NEM 2和NEM 3政策的变化对太阳能用户的影响。NEM 3大幅降低了向PG&E售电的回报率，鼓励用户安装电池以自给自足。尽管电池成本高昂，作者仍成功建立了一个能满足其用电需求的太阳能系统，从而不再受PG&E涨价困扰。

44023226.article_content:
PG&E Sucks or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love Building my own Solar System
Joe Eklund
Follow
24 min read
·
2 days ago
--
5
Listen
Share
W
ell it happened. PG&E has dropped the facade of necessary rate increases because of system upgrades, and they have come out and said what we knew all along:
they only care about profits.
Then they turn around and spit in our faces by telling us our bills are
actually
lower
than they were a year ago
. And if you really want to get your blood boiling, go
read this nonsense from their CEO
.
Last year I got sick of it and started looking at deploying a solar system, and that was before
PG&E decided to have 6 rate hikes (#7 on the way)
. Now a year later, my solar system is up and running, and I no longer cringe anytime I hear the AC kick on in the Bay Area heat (we can’t all live in SF). Here’s how I did it.
Fair warning, I am going to go deep into the weeds on some things. Feel free to skip over sections you find boring or you can even skip to the end if you want to read my lessons learned.
But first, a haiku to summarize the current state of power providers in California:
PG&E sucks
I hate the CPUC
This is all a scam
I received no compensation from any of the companies listed in this article. All thoughts and opinions are my own.
Table of Contents
But Why?
Research
The Build
Lessons Learned
But Why?
I definitely don’t have a problem
Aside from the obvious that PG&E rates are entering ludacris mode, I am a self-hoster. I have a rack in the garage that pulls a little less than 1kw. That’s 1kw 24/7/365. And though I have a garage fan that keeps it cool eight months of the year (and at night), in the summer I have a portable A/C that pulls about 800w when it’s running. It gets hot here, way hotter than what most folks think of when they hear Bay Area. Last summer there were months of an electrical bill north of $1200. Yikes.
You may now be thinking, well why do I need a rack that pulls 1kw? I guess I don’t, but the word
downsize
is not in my vocabulary. Maybe I’ll go over my self-hosting setup in some future articles if there is interest.
Research
Information Overload
As I began researching, it became apparent there were two paths I could take: a small system to offset my constant rack usage or a large system to reduce my need for PG&E (electricity at least — gas is another story) as much as possible.
The rabbit hole then started going deeper: Do it myself? Have a company do it? Batteries? Enphase? Microinverters? Monofacial/Bifacial panels? What is NEM 2/3? How do I rack the panels? Inside or outside the garage for batteries? City planning and inspection? The list goes on and on and can be overwhelming.
Eventually I decided that I wanted a full system to try and completely kill my electricity bill, not just a small system to offset the rack usage.
I figured the next step was to get some quotes for systems from local solar companies. Even if I ended up doing it myself, I could see ballpark pricing and see what kind of system they recommended. I found three companies and gave them my PG&E usage for the past year (about 16,000 kwh) and got three quotes ranging from ~45 — 55k.
But the catch was those systems all drastically undersized the battery in my opinion: they ranged from 5 — 15kwh. In the summer (when electricity is even more expensive), my rack + portable A/C + house A/C (3 ton) could easily be pulling 6kw. That’s not even accounting for other appliances like the microwave or stove.
I could easily burn through the batteries in just a few hours. This
would
at least stop me from pulling power during peak cost TOU hours (4–9PM), but the rest of the night I’d be pulling from PG&E. Also, once you go solar/batteries you actually have a wider time period of peak pricing, called partial peak, that goes all the way to midnight —
E-ELEC
. Now is a good time to talk about
Net Energy Metering (NEM)
.
Net Energy Metering (NEM)
NEM is the agreement you have with PG&E that takes into account the energy you generate and the energy you use. Before 2017, customers would be on NEM 1, which offered the best incentives: free connection and the best export rates. Between 2017 and 2023 customers who installed new solar systems were put on NEM 2. There were a few additional costs passed onto consumers like slightly increased connection fees, but the actual rate you received from PG&E for your generation was the same. Then NEM 3 came in 2023 and the main changes were further increased connection fees and reduced export rates (by about 75%). Eventually everyone will be bumped to NEM 3, but many folks are grandfathered in on NEM 2 for 10–20 years.
NEM 3 means when you generate electricity, PG&E will pay you pennies on the dollar, then turn around and sell it back to you at inflated costs when you are no longer producing solar (i.e. at night).
The solution to this is to install a battery system, but batteries are
expensive
. Really expensive. Though I didn’t proceed with additional quotes fo

data.title: Robin: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
data.author: nopinsight
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为Robin的多代理系统，该系统能够自动化科学发现的关键 intellectual 步骤。Robin通过整合文献检索代理和数据分析代理，能够生成假设、提出实验、解释实验结果并更新假设，从而实现科学发现的半自主化。应用该系统，研究团队发现了一种治疗干性年龄相关黄斑变性（dAMD）的新疗法。Robin提出了增强视网膜色素上皮细胞吞噬功能的治疗策略，并识别和验证了一种有前景的候选药物ripasudil。该药物是一种临床使用的rho激酶（ROCK）抑制剂，此前未被提议用于治疗dAMD。Robin通过提出并分析后续RNA测序实验，揭示了ripasudil上调吞噬功能的机制。该研究展示了Robin作为首个在迭代实验室框架内自主发现并验证新治疗候选药物的AI系统，为AI驱动的科学发现建立了新范式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在科学研究中的应用及其潜力和局限

不同观点：
• [greenflag] 提到AI系统所谓的“新发现”实际上已经有相关综述文章，质疑其创新性。通过引用Twitter上的讨论，指出现有研究可能已经被充分探讨，AI只是重新发现了已知内容。

• [hirenj] 对AI发现持谨慎态度，指出已有研究通过GWAS（全基因组关联研究）排除了AI发现基因（ABCA1）的作用，认为如果只是重新利用已有数据并进行常规实验（如RNA-seq），并不会引起太大兴趣。同时，对AI系统能否真正带来新的科研突破表示怀疑。

• [ankit219] 关注AI在生物科技和制药领域的实际应用，提出模型在面对未公开研究数据和失败实验时的局限性，尤其是模型对未知信息的猜测可能导致不准确。同时，对AI在科研工作中的角色提出疑问，是作为协同研究者还是深度参与日常工作流程。

View a PDF of the paper titled Robin: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery, by Ali Essam Ghareeb and 9 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Scientific discovery is driven by the iterative process of background research, hypothesis generation, experimentation, and data analysis. Despite recent advancements in applying artificial intelligence to scientific discovery, no system has yet automated all of these stages in a single workflow. Here, we introduce Robin, the first multi-agent system capable of fully automating the key intellectual steps of the scientific process. By integrating literature search agents with data analysis agents, Robin can generate hypotheses, propose experiments, interpret experimental results, and generate updated hypotheses, achieving a semi-autonomous approach to scientific discovery. By applying this system, we were able to identify a novel treatment for dry age-related macular degeneration (dAMD), the major cause of blindness in the developed world. Robin proposed enhancing retinal pigment epithelium phagocytosis as a therapeutic strategy, and identified and validated a promising therapeutic candidate, ripasudil. Ripasudil is a clinically-used rho kinase (ROCK) inhibitor that has never previously been proposed for treating dAMD. To elucidate the mechanism of ripasudil-induced upregulation of phagocytosis, Robin then proposed and analyzed a follow-up RNA-seq experiment, which revealed upregulation of ABCA1, a critical lipid efflux pump and possible novel target. All hypotheses, experimental plans, data analyses, and data figures in the main text of this report were produced by Robin. As the first AI system to autonomously discover and validate a novel therapeutic candidate within an iterative lab-in-the-loop framework, Robin establishes a new paradigm for AI-driven scientific discovery.

44043323.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为Robin的多代理系统，该系统能够自动化科学发现的关键 intellectual 步骤。Robin通过整合文献检索代理和数据分析代理，能够生成假设、提出实验、解释实验结果并更新假设，从而实现科学发现的半自主化。应用该系统，研究团队发现了一种治疗干性年龄相关黄斑变性（dAMD）的新疗法。Robin提出了增强视网膜色素上皮细胞吞噬功能的治疗策略，并识别和验证了一种有前景的候选药物ripasudil。该药物是一种临床使用的rho激酶（ROCK）抑制剂，此前未被提议用于治疗dAMD。Robin通过提出并分析后续RNA测序实验，揭示了ripasudil上调吞噬功能的机制。该研究展示了Robin作为首个在迭代实验室框架内自主发现并验证新治疗候选药物的AI系统，为AI驱动的科学发现建立了新范式。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了奥地利作家罗伯特·穆齐尔（Robert Musil）在1921至1924年间作为剧评家和剧作家的创作与思想生活，特别是他的两部剧作《乌托邦者》和《文森兹与重要人物的情妇》。穆齐尔对当时剧场作品的负面评价促使他创作了这两部剧，以表达他对剧场问题的思考和回应。《乌托邦者》花费十年完成，被穆齐尔视为重要作品，而《文森兹与重要人物的情妇》则仅用14天写成，是一部讽刺喜剧。这两部剧作反映了他对乌托邦思想的探索，尤其是“下一步乌托邦”的概念，强调对僵化系统和习惯的反抗，追求创造性和开放性。这种思想也贯穿于他未完成的小说《没有个性的人》中，体现了穆齐尔对艺术在社会中核心角色的重视。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对《没有个性的人》这本书的评价和理解存在分歧，特别是其是否无聊以及是否需要特定的文学背景才能欣赏。

不同观点：
• [nyeah] 认为《没有个性的人》非常无聊，并在阅读英文译本时感到困惑，质疑是否错过了某些关键点或技巧。
• [LitLover] 认为《没有个性的人》是杰作，但承认这本书需要读者具备一定的文学背景和耐心。它指出，这本书探讨了复杂的哲学主题，可能不适合所有读者。
• [Reader1984] 同意[nyeah]的观点，表示自己也在英文译本中感到迷失，认为翻译可能没有传达出原文的微妙之处。

补充讨论：
• 一些读者如[LitLover]强调，阅读这类文学作品时，理解历史和文化背景有助于更好地欣赏作品。
• [Reader1984]指出，翻译质量可能影响阅读体验，建议尝试不同的译本或直接阅读德文原版。
• 争议的焦点在于《没有个性的人》是否本质上就是枯燥的，还是读者需要具备特定知识或选择更好的译本才能欣赏。

总结：评论中对《没有个性的人》的看法两极分化，一部分读者认为其枯燥难懂，另一部分则认为其价值在于深刻的哲学探讨，并强调文学背景和译本选择的重要性。

The Austrian Writer Whose Forgotten Plays Inspired His Greatest Work of Fiction
Genese Grill on Robert Musil's Intellectual and Creative Life
By
Genese Grill
December 17, 2020
The years 1921 to 1924 constituted the height of Robert Musil’s participation in the world of theater as both critic and dramatist. He later had plans to collect his writings on theater into a book, which he considered calling
Pathology of the Theater
or
Theater from the Outside
. In one notebook entry, he writes that “A pathologist would be able to diagnose a great deal about our time through the theater.”

According to his own avowal, Musil was spurred on to the writing of his two finished plays,
The Utopians
and
Vinzenz and the Mistress of Important Men
, by his negative assessment of the contemporary offerings.
The Utopians
(1921)—which took him approximately ten years to write and which he considered one of his major works—was written, he explained, to “finally, for once, bring some spirit into the controversies surrounding the theater.” It was awarded the prestigious Kleist Prize almost immediately, but was only premiered in 1929, against Musil’s wishes, under the directorship of Jo Lhehrman—a con-man who could almost have come right out of one of Musil’s own plays. Of the second,
Vinzenz and the Mistress of Important Men
(1923)—a farce that was performed to enthusiastic audiences even before its publication in book form—he reported, “[B]ecause, for once, it just all finally got to be too stupid, I have written a play in 14 days.” Both were written in tandem with his close analysis of contemporary theater and as partial answers to the problems this analysis posed.
We know that late drafts for
The Man without Qualities
are rife with a variety of utopias, which the author in extremis considered as possible endings for the unfinished (unfinishable) novel. None was more favored than his “utopia of the next step,” a mode of life and thought prefigured in
The Utopians
and in
Vinzenz and the Mistress of Important Men
, whereby an action may only be judged by what it brings in its wake, ad infinitum. This utopian state constitutes a radical resistance to closure and final conclusion, manifest in a life of creative aliveness and presence that is represented by another of Musil’s favored utopias: the “Utopia of the Motivated Life.” As Albrecht Schöne pointed out in his brilliant essay on the use of the subjunctive in Musil’s novel, this mode of thought (like the subjunctive case that expresses it) is anathema to rigid (and declarative) systems.
The utopian thinker, the possibilitarian, would, thus, be the first person to be expelled from any established utopia. An ossified utopia, in other words, is already dystopian. The utopia of the next step is not a place or a fixed system, but a resistance to deadly habit and dull conformity, a creative openness, the only state wherein art can be created and experienced—in effect, a utopia without delusive ideals. As Thomas in
The Utopians
says to an outraged Miss Mertens: “Ideals are dead idealism.” And Musil’s serious engagement with utopian thought, from these early plays and critical writings through the last decade of his life and the last notes for his life’s work, are also a measure of the central social role he assigned to art.
Musil’s two finished plays anticipate the novel’s aesthetic and ethical tension between the self-same and the criminal, creative variations that interrupt its habitual circling. In
The Utopians
, we find a powerful early metaphor for the tension between patterns and creative alternatives, presented later in the novel as the “two dozen cake pans” into which life is too-often poured and thus limited. In the 1921 play, Regina and Thomas talk about the way they used to walk along the patterns in a carpet (now in the house inherited by Thomas and Maria) as children. Thomas laments:

data.title: Improving performance of rav1d video decoder
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了作者如何通过两个小的性能改进，使Rust编写的rav1d视频解码器在macOS M3芯片上比原来快了略超1%。rav1d是C编写的dav1d AV1解码器的Rust移植版本。在此次优化中，作者使用了采样分析器（samply）比较rav1d和dav1d的性能，特别关注汇编优化函数作为锚点。通过函数逐个对比，作者发现并修复了导致性能差异的问题，如不必要的边界检查和Rust特有的低效代码。最终，作者在不引入任何新的不安全代码的前提下，成功地将rav1d的解码速度提高了1%以上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust代码优化及AV1解码器的性能改进

不同观点：
• [mmastrac] 和 [smallpipe] 提到了Rust中比较两个u16数据类型的性能问题，并引用了具体的GitHub问题单链接，讨论了代码优化细节，特别是关于如何避免缓冲区清零的性能提升。
• [nemothekid] 提到了另一篇文章中关于缓冲区清零问题的讨论，并将两篇文章联系起来，暗示这类优化在社区中引起了关注。
• [lubesGordi] 认为第一个优化（通过perf工具发现）是显而易见的，但第二个优化更复杂且有趣，强调了perf工具的价值。
• [tialaramex] 提出了一个更广泛的观点，认为像dav1d这样的编解码器应该用WUFFS等专用语言实现，尽管将现有Rust代码优化可能相对容易，但从长远来看，使用专用语言可能更有意义。
• [renewiltord] 提到了ffmpeg社区对Rust的抵制，并引用了Twitter上的讨论，暗示Rust在多媒体处理领域的应用存在争议。

Making the rav1d Video Decoder 1% Faster
May 22, 2025
rust

performance
*on macOS with an M3 chip
*slightly more than 1%, on a specific benchmark, without any new unsafe code
A while ago,
memorysafety.org announced a contest
for improving performance of
rav1d
, a Rust port of the
dav1d
AV1 decoder.
As this literally has my name written on it, I thought it would be fun to give it a try (even though I
probably
can’t participate in the contest).
This is a write-up about two small performance improvements I found (
1st PR
,
2nd PR
) and how I found them (you can also jump to the
summary in the end
).
Background and Approach
rav1d
is a port of
dav1d
, created by (1) running
c2rust
on
dav1d
, (2) incorporating
dav1d
’s asm-optimized functions, and (3) changing the code to be more Rust-y and safer.
The authors also published
a detailed article
about the process and the performance work they did.
More recently, the contest was announced, with the baseline being:
Our Rust-based rav1d decoder is currently about 5% slower than the C-based dav1d decoder.
Video decoders are notoriously complex pieces of software, but because we are comparing the performance of two similar deterministic binaries we might be able to avoid a lot of that complexity - with the right tooling.
We can’t expect to find huge wins, and some regressions might be too-hard-to-tackle (for example, LLVM finding a Rust function harder to optimize than the C version),
but it’s worth a shot, especially since aarch64 (my environment) is probably less optimized than x86_64.
My approach here was to:
Use a sampling profiler to capture snapshots of both runs on the same input.
Use the optimized asm calls as “anchors” since they should match perfectly.
Compare the Rust and C versions function by function, and if there’s a big enough discrepancy, dive into that function.
Baseline
First things first, we need to build and compare perf locally (using
hyperfine
and the sample files noted in the contest’s rules and
rav1d
’s
CI
).
We’ll be using the single threaded version (
--threads 1
) to keep things simple.
For
rav1d
:

&&
cd
rav1d
&&

data.article_summary: Daniel Huffman介绍了他完成的一个侧项目——绘制《Sid Meier’s Alpha Centauri》游戏中的虚构星球Chiron的地图。该项目极具技术挑战，尤其是从游戏的官方地图中提取数据。地图为128×64像素的钻石形，每个像素包含高度、降雨量、岩石度等多种属性。Huffman逐一记录了8192个地图块的海拔数据，并通过游戏模组获取降雨量信息，最终在QGIS中处理和验证数据。尽管这是虚构地图，但Huffman主要处理现实世界的地理数据，他强调绘制虚构地图与现实地图需要不同的技能。该地图可免费下载，但制作过程耗时费力，他鼓励支持他的工作。
